explanation: The 1954 Hague Convention created the shield to mark monuments, museums and archives. Three orange circles mark dams and nuclear power stations, and a blue triangle on an orange ground marks civil defence.

claims.text: The 1954 Hague Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict created a blue-and-white shield as the emblem of protected cultural property.
The blue-and-white shield does not mark hospitals, dams or nuclear plants, or civil defence; hospitals use the red cross, red crescent or red crystal.
The cultural property emblem marks sites such as monuments, museums and archives.
Under Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions, three bright orange circles mark works containing dangerous forces, such as dams and nuclear power stations.
The international sign of civil defence is a blue equilateral triangle on an orange background.
